name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing and inauthentic network activity on social platforms, spanning the CooRnet/CLSB methodology, the vera.ai WP4 work, and the new VERA-AI Alert monitoring system. This is the researcher's signature methodological contribution and remains the most active line of current publication.

name: Platform Data Access & Governance
description: Research on social media platforms' data-access regimes, API restrictions, and content-moderation/governance policies (e.g. CrowdTangle shutdown, Meta's URL Shares Dataset threshold, political content reduction policy, DSA-era research APIs), including the PI's EU expert-group work on systemic risk assessment under the Digital Services Act.

name: LLMs & Computational Content Analysis
description: Methodological work on applying large language models and embeddings to classify, cluster and annotate political and news content at scale, including validation challenges of LLM-in-the-loop pipelines for communication research — an actively growing empirical/methods agenda.

name: Generative AI & Synthetic Disinformation
description: Study of how generative AI is used to produce and scale deceptive content — synthetic visuals in coordinated gambling promotion, 'zombie' information operations, and iterative deception strategies — reflecting a current pivot of the disinformation research line toward AI-generated media.

name: Italian Electoral Communication
description: Longitudinal mapping of Italian news media and social media dynamics around national elections (2018, 2019 European, 2022), including political parallelism, partisan attention, and coordinated networks — the founding and ongoing core of the MINE research programme.

name: Political Polarization & Partisanship
description: Analysis of partisan community dynamics, insularity, affective engagement and hyperpartisan media networks across platforms, examining how social and traditional media interplay to amplify political polarization.

name: Health Misinformation & Fact-Checking
description: Research mapping coordinated circulation of problematic health information (COVID-19, vaccine discourse) in Italy, India and Nigeria, and tools to accelerate fact-checking workflows, funded through Gates Foundation and Italian MUR grants.

name: Information Disorder & Hybrid Media Theory
description: Conceptual and taxonomic work on misinformation, 'fake news' and information disorder within the hybrid media system, underpinning the researcher's broader empirical programme on disinformation.

name: Latin American Digital Politics
description: Emerging comparative research on political information campaigns and partisan community engagement in Latin America, notably pro-Bolsonaro Facebook networks in Brazil, marking a geographic expansion of the coordinated-behavior and polarization agenda.

name: Social Media Platform Affordances & Engagement
description: Studies of how platform-specific features (Facebook reactions, algorithmic feed governance, second-screen TV engagement) shape user interaction and visibility, connecting older social-TV research to current work on algorithmic curation and engagement metrics.

name: Digital Research Methods Teaching
description: Teaching and training activity in computational social science methods — social network analysis, generative AI applications, R/Python tutorials for media data — reflecting the researcher's role in disseminating digital methods to students and practitioners.

name: Platforms, Audiences, and Online Communities
description: Empirical and reflective studies of how platform affordances, cultures, and audience practices shape online sociality, identity, and community formation across sites like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter/Mastodon, and LiveJournal.

name: Critical Analysis of AI Industry Imaginaries and Discourse
description: Studies examining how AI industry actors, media, and communities construct and circulate narratives, imaginaries, and framings (e.g., longtermism, techno-hagiography, 'quiet futuring', political-economy 'decoys') that shape public understanding and obscure or legitimize the underlying power structures of AI development.

name: Reflections on the State of Misinformation and Online Harm Research
description: Papers that step back from primary empirical study to critically assess the misinformation/online-harms research field itself — diagnosing biases (e.g., WEIRD-centrism, overreliance on cognitive proxies), mapping gaps in evidence (causal, longitudinal, cross-national), and proposing directions or borrowed lessons (e.g., from climate psychology) to make the field more rigorous and generalizable.

name: Theorizing AI's Social Role: Agency, Trust, and Public Perception
description: Papers that apply or extend social theory and communication-trust frameworks to understand the societal position of AI systems, ranging from conceptual demarcations of machine agency and formal multi-agent social frameworks to models of public trust in generative AI and empirical survey data on public attitudes toward AI adoption.

name: Computational Studies of Political Media and Advertising
description: Papers using large-scale computational or quasi-experimental methods to study political advertising, media capture, and ideological signaling on digital platforms, including causal analysis of ad effects, detection of covert advertiser influence on news coverage, and latent ideology estimation of political video content.

name: Survey Measurement Validity and Comparability
description: Papers examining methodological challenges in survey-based measurement, including whether respondents understand survey questions as intended, how online sample composition and quality checks affect representativeness and response validity, and how question wording and dataset differences affect cross-national and longitudinal comparability of trust measures.
